# TextOS App Style Guide — V1

**Date:** May 29, 2026
**Status:** Spec locked. Implementation pending.
**Scope:** Every mini-app generated by the v2 apps platform (strategy archetype now; assessment + calculator when they come online).
**Authority:** This document is the single source of truth for both (a) the LLM design-step prompt — what data the model must emit — and (b) the assembler — how that data renders. If implementation diverges from this spec, the implementation is the bug.

---

## 1. The frame (the outer container of every app)

Every generated app sits inside a single visual frame on the page. The frame is what gives apps a unified "TextOS app" identity regardless of business or archetype.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Max width (desktop) | 768px |
| Horizontal centering | Yes, on the page |
| Corner radius | 16px |
| Border | 1px solid `#e5e7eb` |
| Shadow | Medium drop shadow (Bootstrap `shadow` utility — between `shadow-sm` and `shadow-lg`) |
| Inner background | `#ffffff` (pure white) |
| Inner padding | 32px on desktop, 20px on mobile |
| Page background (outside the frame) | Soft gray `#f5f5f7` (current page background) |

Implementation: a single `<div class="textos-app-frame">` wraps the entire app body. Class is defined in the assembler's emitted stylesheet, not in user content. Frame is invariant across archetypes.

---

## 2. The hero (top of every app)

No card. No dark band. No background fill of any kind. Just typography stacked vertically.

Structure, top to bottom:

1. **Tabler icon.** ~48px, primary color, centered. LLM picks the icon slug per app (examples: `bar-chart` for assessments, `target` for strategy, `calculator` for math, `chef-hat` for food businesses, `list-check` for planners, `compass` for direction-finding apps).
2. **Title.** ~28px, weight 600, dark text color, centered. The app's name as the LLM generated it.
3. **Tagline.** ~16px, muted gray (`#6b7280`), centered, max-width constrained so it doesn't span the full frame width.

No icon background, no border around the icon, no decorative bar. The icon's color and the title's weight are the only visual hooks.

Spacing: ~16px between icon and title, ~8px between title and tagline, ~32px between tagline and the next component below.

---

## 3. The wizard (multi-step input)

The Homer `c_wizard` component renders the input flow, but we configure it to suppress per-step tab labels and surface a progress indicator instead.

### Step labels
Suppressed. The wizard's tab nav (the "Step 1 / Step 2 / Step 3" row) is hidden via CSS. The user's progress is communicated through:

- A horizontal progress bar at the top of the wizard area
- A text counter immediately below it: "Question 3 of 7"

The counter is dynamic — updates as the user moves between steps. Implemented in the assembler's emitted JS, hooked into the existing `form-wizard.js` step-change event.

### Step composition
**One question per step.** No stacking questions on the same step (the current build is putting 2-3 on step 1, which is why it feels rushed and bad). The LLM emits `questions: [...]` and the assembler creates one wizard step per question. The email-capture is always the final step.

### Navigation buttons (bottom of each step)
- **Back** — text-only link, left-aligned, muted gray. Hidden on the first step.
- **Next** — solid primary button, right-aligned. Hidden on the last step.
- **Submit** (last step only) — solid success/primary button, right-aligned, text "Get My [Result Noun]" where the LLM picks the result noun per app (e.g., "Get My Strategy", "Get My Plan", "Get My Recommendation").

---

## 4. Radio cards (the question option style)

Every multiple-choice question uses the rich radio-card variant.

### Shape per option
Each option is a card with three pieces stacked or arranged:
- **Tabler icon** (left, ~24px, primary color when selected, muted when not)
- **Label** (bold, primary text color)
- **Description** (small, muted gray, single line, optional — LLM chooses to emit or skip)

### States
- **Rest:** white background, 1px subtle gray border (`#e5e7eb`), muted icon
- **Hover:** light gray fill (`#f9fafb`), primary-color border, primary-color icon
- **Selected:** full primary fill, white text, white icon, no border (or border same color as fill)

### Layout
Two cards per row on desktop (the existing `col-md-6` pattern from Homer). One per row on mobile.

### LLM data contract
The LLM must emit per option:
```json
{
  "label": "Premium restaurants",
  "value": "premium_restaurants",
  "icon": "tools-kitchen-2",
  "description": "High-end establishments seeking artisan products"
}
```
`icon` is a Tabler icon slug. `description` is optional but encouraged. `label` and `value` are required.

---

## 5. Text input + textarea + email input

Standard Homer styling. No customization needed beyond what's in the catalog. The frame (Section 1) handles all visual containment — these components sit inside it cleanly.

For the email-capture step specifically: render the email input, then the submit button. Don't add extra explanatory text — the wizard's flow already implies "submit to see your result."

---

## 6. Result phase

The payoff. What the visitor sees after submitting.

### Container
A single `c_card_basic` inside the same outer frame as the wizard was. The result replaces the wizard in the DOM (wizard hidden, result revealed) — same frame, different content.

### Top of the result card: hero image
fal.ai-generated banner image, 1024×512 (2:1 aspect), corner-radius matching the card. **Generated once per app at build time** (not per-result, not per-visitor). The image prompt is picked by the LLM based on the business and the archetype — for the charcuterie strategy app, something like "rustic artisan charcuterie board in warm light, editorial photography style."

The image is baked into the result HTML at app generation. No fal.ai call on result reveal.

### Below the image
- **Headline result.** ~32px, weight 700. One line. E.g., "Your Strategic Growth Plan", "Your Custom Charcuterie Board", "Your Marketing Roadmap".
- **One-paragraph summary.** ~16px, muted gray. The "here's what we recommend" paragraph.
- **Sections.** Multiple stacked sub-sections inside the result card. Each section has a small heading + body text. LLM emits 3-5 sections per result. Examples for strategy archetype:
  - "Your Audience" — paragraph summarizing target market
  - "Your Differentiator" — paragraph summarizing positioning
  - "Your Next Three Moves" — bulleted list of recommended actions
  - "Your 30-Day Plan" — week-by-week breakdown
- **CTA section at the bottom.** Per the PRD's component-quality guidelines, every result ends with a `c_card_cta` block — primary CTA (e.g., "Talk to us about implementing this") and a quieter secondary action (e.g., "Save this plan as PDF").

---

## 7. Color palette

Fixed across all apps. No per-business theming in V1.

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| `--primary` | Homer default green (current) | Action buttons, selected radio cards, accent icons, links |
| `--text` | `#1f2937` | Body text, titles |
| `--text-muted` | `#6b7280` | Taglines, descriptions, helper text |
| `--bg-page` | `#f5f5f7` | Outside the frame |
| `--bg-frame` | `#ffffff` | Inside the frame |
| `--border` | `#e5e7eb` | Frame border, input borders, radio-card rest border |
| `--success` | Homer default success | Confirmation states |
| `--danger` | Homer default danger | Error states |

The primary stays Homer's default green for now. Decision documented; revisit post-launch.

---

## 8. Dark mode

Respect the visitor's OS preference via `<html data-bs-theme="light">` or `"dark"`, set from `prefers-color-scheme` media query in the assembler's emitted bootstrap script.

| Token | Light | Dark |
|---|---|---|
| `--bg-page` | `#f5f5f7` | `#0a0a0a` |
| `--bg-frame` | `#ffffff` | `#1a1a1a` |
| `--text` | `#1f2937` | `#f3f4f6` |
| `--text-muted` | `#6b7280` | `#9ca3af` |
| `--border` | `#e5e7eb` | `#374151` |
| `--primary` | (Homer green) | (Homer green, slightly lifted) |

Shadow: keep the drop shadow visible in dark mode by switching to a darker, denser shadow color (Bootstrap handles this if we use the `shadow` utility correctly).

Bootstrap 5's `data-bs-theme` handles the bulk of token swapping. We only need to override the few tokens above that aren't Bootstrap defaults.

---

## 9. Typography

| Element | Font | Size | Weight |
|---|---|---|---|
| Hero title | System sans (Inter/system-ui) | 28px | 600 |
| Hero tagline | System sans | 16px | 400 |
| Question text | System sans | 18px | 500 |
| Radio card label | System sans | 16px | 600 |
| Radio card description | System sans | 13px | 400 |
| Result headline | System sans | 32px | 700 |
| Result section heading | System sans | 20px | 600 |
| Body / paragraph text | System sans | 16px | 400 |
| Button text | System sans | 15px | 600 |

System sans = `-apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif`. Generated apps don't load Bebas Neue — that's TextOS dashboard brand, not visitor-facing app brand.

---

## 10. Spacing

| Context | Value |
|---|---|
| Page padding (around the frame) | 32px on desktop, 16px on mobile |
| Frame inner padding | 32px desktop, 20px mobile |
| Hero icon → title | 16px |
| Hero title → tagline | 8px |
| Hero → first component | 32px |
| Between major components inside frame | 32px |
| Between radio cards | 12px |
| Between wizard steps' content blocks | 24px |
| Between result sections | 24px |

---

## 11. Animation + interaction

Minimal. The wizard's tab-pane transition (Homer default Bootstrap fade ~150ms) is the only motion. No scroll animations, no parallax, no fancy reveals. The visitor's attention should be on the content, not the chrome.

Radio cards: 100ms color transition on hover/select.

Form-wizard.js handles step transitions natively. Don't add custom transitions on top.

---

## 12. Mobile

Every app is mobile-first. Frame collapses to full-width with 16px horizontal page padding. Radio cards stack one-per-row. Hero stays centered, type sizes scale down ~15%.

Bootstrap 5 handles the breakpoints. We use `col-12 col-md-6` patterns for radio cards. Frame's `max-width: 768px` paired with `width: 100%` handles the desktop/mobile sizing.

---

## 13. LLM data contract — what the design-step prompt must produce

The full composition spec the LLM emits per app build:

```json
{
  "app_type": "strategy",
  "app_title": "Gaudet Charcuterie Strategic Growth Planner",
  "app_tagline": "Identify growth opportunities and craft your winning market strategy",
  "hero_icon": "target",
  "image_prompt": "rustic artisan charcuterie board with cured meats and cheeses in warm editorial lighting, photographed from above",
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q1",
      "type": "radio",
      "text": "What is your primary customer base?",
      "options": [
        {
          "label": "Premium restaurants",
          "value": "premium_restaurants",
          "icon": "tools-kitchen-2",
          "description": "High-end establishments seeking artisan products"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      "id": "q2",
      "type": "textarea",
      "text": "What is your biggest operational challenge?",
      "placeholder": "Describe in a few sentences..."
    }
  ],
  "submit_button_text": "Get My Strategy",
  "result": {
    "headline": "Your Strategic Growth Plan",
    "summary": "Based on your inputs, the most leveraged path forward is...",
    "sections": [
      {
        "heading": "Your Audience",
        "body": "Your target market is..."
      }
    ],
    "cta": {
      "primary_text": "Talk to us about implementing this",
      "primary_action": "...",
      "secondary_text": "Save as PDF",
      "secondary_action": "..."
    }
  }
}
```

Required fields: `app_title`, `app_tagline`, `hero_icon`, `image_prompt`, `questions[]`, `submit_button_text`, `result.headline`, `result.summary`, `result.sections[]`, `result.cta`.

Per the no-fallbacks rule: if any required field is missing, the build halts. The assembler does not synthesize defaults.

---

## 14. What this spec does NOT cover (deferred)

- Per-business color theming (V1.1 — currently fixed Homer green)
- fal.ai per-result personalized imagery (V1.1+ — currently per-app build-time)
- Animations beyond fade transitions
- A11y audit beyond Homer defaults
- Print stylesheet
- Saved/returning-visitor states
- Assessment + Calculator archetype specifics (this spec is strategy-only; the other two are stopgaps until generalized)

---

## 15. How to verify a build matches this spec

The visual checklist for every generated app:

- [ ] Single white card with rounded corners, subtle border, drop shadow, centered on a soft-gray page
- [ ] Hero is text-only with a Tabler icon above, centered
- [ ] Wizard has a progress bar + "Question N of M" counter, no tab labels
- [ ] Each question is on its own step (one question per step)
- [ ] Radio cards have icon + bold label + description, three states clear
- [ ] Back is a text link on the left, Next is a solid button on the right
- [ ] Last step has the LLM-named submit button (not generic "Submit")
- [ ] Result has fal.ai banner image at top, headline below, sections stacked, CTA at bottom
- [ ] Dark mode honored if visitor OS prefers it
- [ ] Mobile collapses cleanly, radio cards stack, type scales

If any of these fails on a fresh build, that's a bug.

---

*End of spec.*
